messages:
mike-customer: Hey team — getting 403s and very high TTFB on POST /v1/generate for a few users. Request IDs: rq_7f9a2b3c, rq_7f9a2b7d. Can share payloads if needed but need PII removed.

sara-support: Thanks Mike. Can you confirm account id and approximate timestamps? We’ll need a repro curl and the two request IDs you listed.

mike-customer: Account acct_98123, incidents between 2026-03-15 18:22 and 18:28 UTC. The payloads contain customer names and short notes — I can sanitize but want to follow your recommended flow.

sara-support: OK. If you can redacted-copy the prompt replacing names with [PERSON] and emails with [EMAIL] that’s ideal. Also include the exact Authorization header used (with token masked) and the full response body for the failed requests.

mike-customer: Here’s a sanitized curl I prepared:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"Hello [PERSON], your case #CASE123 needs review."}'
```
I removed PHI but left case ids.

jon-eng: Thanks. Could you also add the runtime headers from the original request (X-Request-Id, X-Region, X-Client-Version). That helps correlate with our logs. If you prefer, we can accept a debug bundle instead of raw logs.

mike-customer: I can grab headers. For the debug bundle — what’s the safest way to share?

alice-privacy: Quick note: do not paste real PII into threads. For bundles use the support upload form link we provided earlier which supports one-way encryption and automatic PII scrub suggestions. If sending via our upload, include a line with what was redacted and why (e.g., replaced 3 names, removed two emails).

jon-eng: If you need to produce a local debug bundle, run: 
```bash
redwood-cli collect-debug --request-ids rq_7f9a2b3c,rq_7f9a2b7d --include-headers --mask-keys Authorization,Email --output debug-rq-190123.tar.gz
```
Then check the bundle with `redwood-cli scrub-check debug-rq-190123.tar.gz` to see suggested redactions.

mike-customer: Running now. One question: will `scrub-check` remove case numbers like CASE123? They are customer-facing but may map to PII.

alice-privacy: scrub-check will flag patterned identifiers. If you want to keep case numbers, mark them in the bundle manifest as non-PII, but note that if they map to internal identifiers we may still request pseudonymization. Best practice: replace with CASE_[NUM].

mike-customer: upload link: https://uploads.redwood.ai/safe/AA23. I uploaded debug-rq-190123.tar.gz and added a README describing replacements: names -> [PERSON], emails -> [EMAIL], case ids -> CASE_[NUM].

debug-bot: Upload received (upload_0a9c). Processing PII scan. Found 2 unmasked email-like strings in logs; flagged for manual review.

jon-eng: I’ll pick this up once the bot finishes. If unmasked emails are present please either re-upload with them masked or grant us ephemeral access to the file for triage. We prefer re-upload with masks.

mike-customer: Understood. I re-run the scrub and re-uploaded as upload_0a9d. No emails now.

debug-bot: Re-scan complete. No PII detected. Correlating request IDs to backend traces now.

jon-eng: Quick findings: both request IDs show auth failures in our gateway (403) with longer backend handshake time causing the TTFB spike. Looks like token introspection timed out once per request. I'll open an eng ticket and attach traces.

sara-support: Thanks Jon. Mike — we’ll follow up with a summary and recommended mitigation (rotate tokens, retry policy). For the billing angle — I don’t see errors tied to billing limits yet but I’ll check account usage and follow up if anything looks off.

mike-customer: Appreciate it. Could you also send the minimal repro curl you used internally? I want to test in our staging before rotating tokens.

jon-eng: Repro curl (internal sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx-INT-REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: rq_7f9a2b3c" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"Hello [PERSON]"}'
```
This should reproduce the 403 when run against the same token state.

sara-support: Filing a support follow-up with summary + action items for Mike: 1) rotate token, 2) re-run curl test, 3) confirm no billing spikes. Expect update in ~2 hours. :calendar:

mike-customer: Got it — thanks team. cc @alice-privacy for paperwork on the scrub.

alice-privacy: Thanks Mike. I logged retention and scrub notes in the privacy ticket. If you want a signed NDA for deeper traces let me know.

jon-eng: Closing loop — eng ticket #ENG-5489 created, will update with root cause post RCA.

sara-support: Marking thread resolved once Mike confirms tests. :white_check_mark:
